claim: Minett UNESCO Biosphere was officially designated on 28 October 2020 and is the first and only biosphere reserve in Luxembourg, covering 11 southern municipalities including Esch-sur-Alzette, Differdange, Dudelange, Rumelange, Sanem, Pétange, Kayl, Schifflange, Mondercange, Käerjeng and Bettembourg.
quote: The Minett UNESCO Biosphere reserve groups together 11 municipalities: Bettembourg, Differdange, Dudelange, Esch-sur-Alzette, Käerjeng, Kayl, Mondercange, Pétange, Rumelange, Sanem and Schifflange.

claim: The Minett region, also known as the Terres rouges (Red Rocks), is densely populated and shaped by iron mining and the steel industry from the late 19th century until the 1990s, with reclaimed brownfields now serving biodiversity.
quote: The region has been strongly affected by industrial activity from the late 19th century until the 1990s: the extraction and processing of iron ore, the iron and steel wastelands as well as the mines have left their mark on the landscape.

claim: Belval is a residential and business district two miles west of Esch city centre built on former brownfields and integrates two 300-foot-tall decommissioned blast furnaces (shut down in 1993) now softened by light installations, gardens and reflecting pools.
quote: Belval is a residential and business district two miles west of the Esch city center that sprawls across acres of former brownfields and successfully integrates two gigantic (300-foot-tall) decommissioned blast furnaces.

claim: Belval blast furnace is open self-guided from early April to end of October (Wed–Fri 10–19h, Sat 10–18h, Sun 14–18h); admission is €5 adult, €3 senior, free under-21, and visitors can climb a 40-metre platform overlooking the Cité des Sciences.
quote: Opening hours are from the beginning of April until the end of October; Wednesdays to Fridays from 10am-7pm, Saturdays from 10am-6pm, and Sundays from 2pm-6pm. Admission is 5€

claim: The Massenoire is a refurbished industrial building in Belval — named after the black masses of coke and tar once used to plug blast-furnace tap holes — that hosts rotating exhibitions on Belval and steel-industry heritage under the Fonds Belval.
quote: The Massenoire... denoting the compound used to close the tap hole of the blast furnace... redeveloped by Fonds Belval into a venue for exhibitions (including 'Belval & More')

claim: The Musée National des Mines de Fer in Rumelange opens its 2026 season on 1 April, runs Thu–Sun in April/May/June/September and Tue–Sun in July/August with three guided departures (14:30, 15:30, 16:30); admission €12 and the underground visit lasts 1h45 at a constant 10 °C.
quote: For individual visitors, the museum is open in April, May, June and September, from Thursday to Sunday with 3 departures at 2:30pm, 3:30pm, and 4:30pm; in July and August, from Tuesday to Sunday

claim: At the Rumelange mining museum, visitors ride a train 90 metres below the surface and walk a 650-metre circuit through tunnels 3 m high and 3–5 m wide in the former Walert/Kirchberg mine, which closed in the 1980s.
quote: The rail terminal, 90 metres below the surface, is the start of a 650-metre circuit through tunnels three metres high and from three to five metres wide.

claim: Train 1900 runs heritage steam trains between Pétange and Fond-de-Gras (25 minutes per route) on Sundays in spring/autumn and additionally Thursdays and Saturdays in summer; fares are €18 first-class / €13 second-class adult, tickets on-site only.
quote: Sundays during spring, autumn, and holidays / Sundays during summer and August 15 / Thursdays during summer / Saturdays during summer... First Class: Adults €18... Second Class: Adults €13

claim: Minett Park Fond-de-Gras is an open-air industrial museum bundling the Fond-de-Gras village (miners' bistro, power station, Victor Binck grocery, station), the Lasauvage mining village, the Giele Botter open-pit and the Celtic oppidum of Titelberg, served by the Train 1900 steam line and the Minièresbunn mine train into France.
quote: Historic buildings include a miners' bistro, power station, old-fashioned grocery store, railway line, railway station, and rail sheds... 'Minièresbunn' mining train takes you from Fond-de-Gras to the mining village of Lasauvage and then to Saulnes (France)

claim: Prënzebierg – Giele Botter is a former open-pit iron-ore landscape turned nature reserve where a 2.5 km discovery trail leads past old mine entrances and fossils, with vegetation reclaiming the once-red minette terrain.
quote: The 2.5-kilometre long hiking trail is all about old mine entrances, open-cast mining in general and also about fossils unearthed during the work. The trail leads through the present-day nature reserve Prënzebierg – Giele Botter.

claim: Ellergronn, 2 km south of Esch-sur-Alzette, is a Natura 2000 reserve on the former Kazebierg iron-ore zone with a visitor centre, the small Mine Cockerill museum, the An der Schmëdd café-restaurant and educational trails of 2.5 / 4.5 / 5 km.
quote: The 'Ellergronn' is part of the European network of nature reserves Natura 2000. Formerly known as the Kazebierg extraction zone, located south of Esch-sur-Alzette, this area was primarily used for iron-ore mining

claim: The Musée National de la Résistance et des Droits Humains on Place de la Résistance in Esch-sur-Alzette reopened in 2022 after renovation that tripled its exhibition space, covering Luxembourg resistance to Nazi occupation, the camps, the fate of Luxembourg's Jews and contemporary human-rights themes.
quote: Permanent Exhibition — Recently expanded to three times its original exhibition space with new museography concepts

claim: Differdange's 1535° Creative Hub — named after iron's melting temperature — is a 16,000 m² conversion of a former ArcelorMittal factory into three buildings housing creative-economy startups, design studios and event spaces.
quote: The 1535° Creative Hub consists of three buildings totaling 16,000m2 located on the site of a former Arcelor Mittal factory in Differdange.

claim: Two-thirds of Belval lies in the municipality of Sanem and the district has been part of the Minett UNESCO Biosphere reserve since 2016, anchoring the University of Luxembourg's Cité des Sciences alongside the preserved blast furnaces.
quote: Since 2016, Belval has been part of the Minett UNESCO Biosphere reserve, dedicated to protecting biodiversity in harmony with sustainable urban development. Belval is a district on a part of the Esch-Belval steelworks, 2/3 of which are in the Municipality of Sanem.
